name: [WEEKLY] Internet-Exposed AI Agent/LLM Service Spawns Shell or LOLBin After Inbound Connection
description: Detects an interpreter-hosted AI/LLM/MCP service (python, uvicorn, gunicorn, node) that accepts an inbound connection from a public/non-loopback source and then spawns a Unix shell or LOLBin child within a short window — the post-auth-bypass remote-code-execution chain. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of critical advisories all describe unauthenticated reach into agent-execution or management surfaces that the same process then turns into command execution: PraisonAI's Jobs API and unauth MCP connect/SSE endpoints (GHSA-fq2m-6wqh-x44g, GHSA-p75f-6fp4-p57w, GHSA-x227-pf99-vffg), LiteLLM's Host-header auth bypass on management routes (CVE-2026-49468), googleapis/mcp-toolbox's opaque-token bypass (CVE-2026-11718), and @acastellon/auth's spoofable-header bypass (GHSA-gfj5-979r-92pw). The chain spans delivery (exposed 0.0.0.0 listener), exploit (missing/bypassed auth on a critical function), and execution (shell/LOLBin spawned by the service). It fires when the AI service process is the direct parent of an OS command interpreter shortly after a public inbound connection — the signature of agent-exec/command-injection RCE — and does NOT fire on local-loopback agent calls, on the service's own normal subprocess use that isn't a shell/LOLBin, or on shells spawned by non-AI parents. IOC slots (`<c2_domain_list>`, `<sha256_list>`) are placeholders for enrichment, not the detection logic.
